name: International Military Tribunal — Nuremberg
jurisdiction: Crimes against peace; War crimes; Crimes against humanity
jurisdiction_note: First codification of individual criminal responsibility under international law.
landmark_case: Göring et al. — established individual responsibility under international law; no head of state immunity; superior orders not a defence. Foundation of all ICL.
key_cases: 22 defendants incl. Göring, Ribbentrop, Keitel, Hess, Speer, Dönitz. 12 death sentences. Göring suicide before execution. Bormann tried in absentia.
note: Foundational moment for international criminal law. Nuremberg Principles adopted by UNGA 1950. First legal use of 'crimes against humanity'. Rejected both head of state immunity and superior orders defence.
legal_basis: London Charter (8 Aug 1945) · Nuremberg Principles (UNGA Res. 95(I), 1946)

name: International Military Tribunal for the Far East — Tokyo
jurisdiction: Crimes against peace; War crimes; Crimes against humanity
jurisdiction_note: Emperor Hirohito shielded for political reasons — foundational legitimacy problem.
landmark_case: Tojo Hideki conviction — aggressive war confirmed as international crime; but Emperor Hirohito's immunity poisoned legitimacy from the start.
key_cases: 28 defendants. 7 death sentences incl. Tojo, Hirota, Doihara. Classes A (crimes against peace), B (war crimes), C (crimes against humanity).
note: More contested than Nuremberg. Emperor Hirohito granted immunity for political reasons. No charge of sexual slavery/comfort women. Dissent by Judge Pal (India) — foundational critique of victor's justice.
legal_basis: Tokyo Charter (Special Proclamation by General MacArthur, 19 Jan 1946)

name: Subsequent Nuremberg Proceedings (Nuremberg Military Tribunals)
parent_creator: US Military Government — Control Council Law No. 10
jurisdiction: War crimes; Crimes against humanity; Membership in criminal organisation
jurisdiction_note: 12 separate trials. First prosecution of medical professionals, industrialists, lawyers for international crimes.
creation: US Military — Control Council Law No. 10
landmark_case: Doctors' Trial (NMT Case 1) → Nuremberg Code (1947) — foundation of all medical research ethics worldwide. IG Farben Trial — first corporate complicity proceeding.
key_cases: Doctors' Trial (7 executed → Nuremberg Code); Einsatzgruppen Trial (14 death sentences, Ohlendorf); Ministries Trial (Weizsäcker); IG Farben; Krupp; Judges' Trial.
note: Extended Nuremberg to industrialists, medical experimenters, judges, SS administrators. Most death sentences commuted under Cold War pressure. Doctors' Trial → Nuremberg Code → Declaration of Helsinki (1964).

name: International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia
jurisdiction: Genocide; Crimes against humanity; War crimes; Grave breaches of 1949 Geneva Conventions
jurisdiction_note: First international criminal court since WWII. Temporal: 1991–. Territorial: former Yugoslavia.
landmark_case: Krstić (2001) — first international judgment confirming Srebrenica as genocide. Kunarac (2001) — rape and sexual slavery as standalone war crimes and crimes against humanity.
key_cases: Milošević (died in custody 2006), Karadžić (40yr), Mladić (life), Gotovina (acquitted on appeal), Tadić (first case), Krstić (genocide/Srebrenica).
stats: 161 indicted; 90 convicted; 19 acquitted; 13 referred to national
note: First international criminal tribunal since WWII. Established rape as crime against humanity (Furundžija); genocide in Srebrenica (Krstić); JCE doctrine; command responsibility standards. Milošević: first sitting head of state indicted.

name: International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda
jurisdiction: Genocide; Crimes against humanity; War crimes (Common Article 3 and AP II)
jurisdiction_note: First international tribunal created specifically to prosecute genocide. Temporal: 1 Jan – 31 Dec 1994.
landmark_case: Akayesu (1998) — first ever international conviction for genocide. Established rape as act of genocide. First definition of rape under international law.
key_cases: Akayesu (first genocide conviction, 1998); Kambanda (first head of government to plead guilty to genocide); Bagosora (life); Nahimana/RTLM (incitement via mass media).
note: First international genocide conviction (Akayesu 1998). Established rape as act of genocide; incitement through mass media (Nahimana). Criticised for failing to prosecute RPF crimes.

name: International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals
jurisdiction: Residual functions of ICTY and ICTR
jurisdiction_note: Appellate jurisdiction, fugitive tracking, sentence enforcement supervision, witness protection.
landmark_case: Kabuga arrest (2020) — RTLM genocide radio founder arrested in Paris at 84, oldest genocide suspect to face international trial. Mladić life sentence affirmed (2021).
key_cases: Mladić appeal (life affirmed, 2021); Stanišić & Simatović retrial (convicted 2021); Félicien Kabuga (arrested 2020, trial ongoing).
stats: 1 active trial (Kabuga); 2 branches; 18 sentence enforcement states
note: Created for residual functions too important to abandon. Tracks remaining fugitives. Supervises sentence enforcement in 18 states.

name: International Criminal Court
parent_creator: Assembly of States Parties (124 states parties)
jurisdiction: Genocide; Crimes against humanity; War crimes; Crime of aggression (2018)
jurisdiction_note: Complementarity principle. Temporal: from 1 July 2002. Crime of aggression activated 2018.
landmark_case: Putin arrest warrant (March 2023) — first warrant against a permanent UNSC member head of state. Lubanga (2012) — first ICC conviction + first reparations orders in international history.
key_cases: Lubanga (first conviction 2012), Al-Mahdi (Timbuktu, 2016), Ntaganda (18yr, 2019), Ongwen (25yr, 2021), Putin + Lvova-Belova (March 2023), Netanyahu + Gallant (Nov 2024).
note: Only permanent international criminal court. Complementarity. No head of state immunity (Art. 27). Full victim participation (Art. 68) and reparations (Art. 75). Netanyahu/Gallant — first democratic state leader. Putin — first UNSC P5 head of state.
legal_basis: Rome Statute (adopted 17 Jul 1998, in force 1 Jul 2002)

name: Special Panels for Serious Crimes — East Timor
jurisdiction: Genocide; Crimes against humanity; War crimes; Domestic serious crimes
jurisdiction_note: Temporal: 1 Jan – 25 Oct 1999. Indonesian occupation and 1999 referendum violence.
landmark_case: Emblematic impunity gap — Wiranto indicted but no extradition obtained. Zero accountability for those most responsible. Model for what not to do in hybrid court design.
key_cases: Wiranto (Indonesian general) indicted — no extradition. 87 convictions largely low-level. Joni Marques (9 convicted).
note: Major structural failure: Indonesia refused extradition of senior officers. Heavily under-resourced. CAVR truth commission ran parallel. No accountability for those most responsible.

name: Regulation 64 Panels — Kosovo (UNMIK)
jurisdiction: War crimes; Crimes against humanity; Serious crimes
jurisdiction_note: Mixed panels: international + Kosovo judges. Political sensitivity around KLA prosecutions.
landmark_case: Demonstrated limits of internationalized panels under UN mission — KLA crimes largely unaddressed, directly necessitating the later Kosovo Specialist Chambers.
key_cases: War crimes and post-conflict ethnically motivated crimes. Limited KLA accountability. Succeeded by KSC.
note: International judges brought in for impartiality — particularly KLA cases. Persistent politicisation. Laid groundwork for KSC.

name: Special Court for Sierra Leone / Residual Special Court
jurisdiction: Crimes against humanity; War crimes; Other serious violations of IHL
jurisdiction_note: Temporal: 30 Nov 1996–. Personal: those bearing greatest responsibility.
landmark_case: Charles Taylor (2012) — first conviction of a former head of state by international tribunal since Nuremberg. Set global precedent that heads of state have no immunity post-tenure.
key_cases: Charles Taylor (50yr, upheld 2013 — first HoS conviction by international tribunal); AFRC, RUF, CDF trials.
stats: 22 indicted; 9 convicted; 2 died during proceedings; 50yr Taylor sentence upheld
note: First international court to sit in the country where crimes occurred. Taylor conviction: first HoS conviction since Nuremberg. Pioneered prosecution of child soldiers, sexual slavery. No reparations jurisdiction.
legal_basis: Agreement between UN and Sierra Leone (16 Jan 2002) · UNSC Res. 1315 (2000)

name: Iraqi High Tribunal
jurisdiction: Genocide; Crimes against humanity; War crimes
jurisdiction_note: No international judges — domestic with international assistance. Temporal: 17 July 1968 – 1 May 2003.
landmark_case: Saddam Hussein executed 30 December 2006 — but before the Anfal/Kurdish genocide trial concluded, denying Kurdish victims full justice.
key_cases: Saddam Hussein (executed Dec 2006 — Dujail conviction, Anfal unfinished); Chemical Ali (executed 2010); Tariq Aziz (died in custody 2015).
stats: 12 senior officials tried; 8 death sentences; 2006 Saddam executed
note: Deeply controversial: established under US-led CPA; Saddam executed before Anfal genocide trial concluded; defence lawyers murdered; proceedings widely criticised for lack of due process.
legal_basis: CPA Order 48 (2003) · Law No. 10 of 2005 (IHT Law)

name: War Crimes Chamber — Court of Bosnia and Herzegovina
jurisdiction: War crimes; Crimes against humanity; Genocide
jurisdiction_note: Cases referred from ICTY under Rule 11 bis. International judges phased out 2013.
landmark_case: Most active war crimes court in world by volume — over 400 cases processed. Demonstrates sustainable domestic complementarity model, but also its limits under political obstruction.
key_cases: Hundreds of Srebrenica perpetrators referred from ICTY. Backlog crisis ongoing.
note: Most active war crimes court by volume. Receives ICTY Rule 11 bis referrals. Unsustainable backlog of 600+ unresolved cases. Dodik/RS political obstruction ongoing.
legal_basis: Law on the Court of BiH (2000, amended 2002) · ICTY Rule 11 bis

name: Extraordinary Chambers in the Courts of Cambodia
jurisdiction: Genocide; Crimes against humanity; War crimes; Domestic crimes
jurisdiction_note: Temporal: 17 Apr 1975 – 6 Jan 1979 (Khmer Rouge period). 40+ years after crimes.
victim_participation: Civil party (3,800+ civil parties in Case 002)
landmark_case: Duch (Case 001, 2010) — first conviction. Civil party model with 3,800+ participants directly inspired ICC victim participation design. Most expensive tribunal per conviction in history.
key_cases: Case 001: Duch (S-21 commander, life, died 2020). Case 002: Nuon Chea + Khieu Samphan (life 2014/2022). Cases 003/004 stalled.
stats: 3 convicted; 1 died before verdict; Life all sentences; $300M+ total cost
note: Most expensive international tribunal per conviction. 40+ years after crimes. Civil party model (3,800+ parties) directly influenced ICC reparations design. Cases 003/004 stalled by Cambodian government.

name: Special Tribunal for Lebanon
jurisdiction: Terrorism; Crimes against humanity (if applicable)
jurisdiction_note: First international court with terrorism as primary jurisdiction — applying Lebanese domestic law.
landmark_case: Ayyash et al. (2020) — first international terrorism convictions in absentia. Established that targeted political assassination can be prosecuted internationally. Zero enforcement.
key_cases: Ayyash et al. — four Hezbollah members convicted in absentia for assassination of PM Hariri. Merhi acquitted. Zero defendants ever in custody.
stats: 5 accused; 4 convicted in absentia; 1 acquitted; $1B+ total cost
note: Unique: only international tribunal applying domestic law to terrorism. All convictions in absentia — no enforcement mechanism. Formally completed mandate 31 Dec 2023.

name: Extraordinary African Chambers — Hissène Habré
jurisdiction: Crimes against humanity; War crimes; Torture
jurisdiction_note: Temporal: 7 June 1982 – 1 December 1990. Habré regime crimes in Chad.
landmark_case: Habré (2016) — first African court to convict a former African head of state. First conviction anywhere of a head of state for sexual violence. 30 years of victims' advocacy rewarded — then betrayed by non-implementation of reparations.
key_cases: Hissène Habré — convicted May 2016. Life sentence confirmed April 2017. $125M reparations ordered — zero paid.
stats: 1 conviction; Life sentence; ~40,000 victims; $0 reparations paid
note: First African court to convict a former African head of state. First conviction for sexual violence against a head of state. Reparations order completely unimplemented.
legal_basis: AU-Senegal Agreement (22 Aug 2012) · EAC Statute · ICJ, Belgium v. Senegal (2012)

name: Kosovo Specialist Chambers & SPO
jurisdiction: Crimes against humanity; War crimes; Other crimes under Kosovo law
jurisdiction_note: Temporal: 1 Jan 1998 – 31 Dec 2000. KLA members for crimes against Serbs, Roma, political opponents.
landmark_case: Thaçi indictment (2020) — sitting President of Kosovo stepped down to face charges before an international body. Unprecedented in democratic states.
key_cases: Thaçi, Veseli, Mustafa, Rexhaj. Salih Mustafa convicted 26yr (2023). Thaçi trial ongoing.
note: Politically sensitive — prosecutes Kosovo's former liberation movement. Thaçi was President at time of indictment. Sui generis: Kosovo law in The Hague.

name: Special Criminal Court — Central African Republic
jurisdiction: Crimes against humanity; War crimes; Genocide
jurisdiction_note: Mixed bench: CAR + international judges. Operates in active conflict zone.
landmark_case: First verdict (2022) — first African hybrid court to order reparations. 18 reparation measures. First tribunal to operate within a country where crimes are actively ongoing.
key_cases: First verdict 2022: Adoum, Yaouba, Tahir — crimes against humanity, war crimes. Life sentences. 18 reparation measures.
stats: 3 first convictions (2022); Life sentences; 18 reparation measures
note: First tribunal operating in country where crimes are ongoing. First African hybrid court with reparations mandate. Genuine complementarity with ICC.

name: International, Impartial and Independent Mechanism — Syria
jurisdiction: Evidence preservation for crimes against humanity, war crimes, genocide in Syria
jurisdiction_note: Not a court. Created after Russia/China blocked UNSC referral of Syria to ICC.
landmark_case: Supported Anwar Raslan conviction (Germany, 2022) — first conviction anywhere for Assad regime crimes. UNGA breakthrough model for UNSC veto situations.
key_cases: Evidence provided to Germany (Raslan, Koblenz 2022), Sweden, France, Netherlands UJ proceedings.
stats: 100+ national proceedings supported; 2M+ items in archive
note: Created after Russia/China UNSC veto. UNGA resolution — no UNSC consensus required. Does not prosecute — preserves evidence. Model replicated for Myanmar (IIMM).

name: UN Investigative Team for Accountability of Da'esh — Iraq
jurisdiction: Evidence preservation for genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes by ISIS in Iraq
jurisdiction_note: Not a court — supports Iraqi judicial proceedings and UJ proceedings globally.
landmark_case: First systematic UN documentation of Yazidi genocide — established evidentiary foundation for multiple German proceedings.
key_cases: Supports Iraqi courts, German/French/Swedish UJ proceedings (Yazidi genocide), Sinjar and Mosul mass grave documentation.
stats: 70+ national proceedings supported; 200+ mass graves documented
note: Created at Iraq's request — rare UNSC unanimity. Specifically mandated to document Yazidi genocide. Mandate ended 17 Sep 2024 after Iraq declined renewal; archives transferred per UNSC Res. 2697 (2023).
legal_basis: UNSC Res. 2379 (21 Sep 2017); mandate ended UNSC Res. 2697 (2023)

name: Independent Investigative Mechanism for Myanmar
jurisdiction: Evidence preservation for genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes in Myanmar
jurisdiction_note: Not a court. Modelled on IIIM Syria. Established after genocide findings against Rohingya.
landmark_case: Supports Gambia v. Myanmar (ICJ) — first ICJ genocide case with provisional measures against ongoing genocide (2020).
key_cases: Supports Gambia v. Myanmar (ICJ, provisional measures 2020); Argentina UJ proceedings; ICC (limited — via Bangladesh).
stats: 2018 established; ICJ Gambia v. Myanmar supported
note: Established after genocide findings against Rohingya. No UNSC consensus required. Supports Gambia's ICJ case and Argentina UJ prosecution.

name: Independent International Commission of Inquiry on Ukraine
jurisdiction: War crimes; Crimes against humanity; IHL violations — Russia-Ukraine
jurisdiction_note: Fact-finding and documentation. Reports to UNHRC and UNGA.
landmark_case: Child deportation documentation directly supported ICC arrest warrants for Putin and Lvova-Belova (March 2023) — first time a CoI report fed directly into a head of state arrest warrant.
key_cases: Documents Russian strikes on civilian infrastructure, deportations of Ukrainian children, sexual violence, torture.
note: Works alongside ICC investigation and national proceedings. Child deportation findings directly supported ICC warrants.

name: Commission for International Justice and Accountability
jurisdiction: Syrian regime crimes documentation — crimes against humanity, war crimes, genocide
jurisdiction_note: Not a court or UN body. Operates like independent prosecutor — chain-of-custody evidence from regime archives.
landmark_case: Caesar photographs (55,000 images of detainee deaths) + CIJA documents = central evidence in Koblenz Raslan trial (2022), first conviction for Assad regime crimes anywhere.
key_cases: Caesar files central to Koblenz trial. Evidence used in Sweden, Netherlands, Austria.
stats: 800,000+ pages of regime docs; 15+ national proceedings supported
note: Unique model: independent prosecutor without judicial mandate. Pre-dates IIIM. Non-governmental structure allows operational flexibility.
legal_basis: No UN mandate — operates under national disclosure frameworks

name: Special Tribunal for the Crime of Aggression against Ukraine
parent_creator: Council of Europe — Enlarged Partial Agreement / Ukraine
jurisdiction: Crime of aggression — Russian political and military leadership
jurisdiction_note: Fills ICC gap: ICC cannot exercise aggression jurisdiction over Russian nationals. Temporal: from 24 Feb 2022. Personal: senior leadership in a position to control or direct State action.
head_of_state_immunity: Limited (troika immunity for sitting Head of State, Head of Government, Foreign Minister)
creation: Bilateral agreement — Council of Europe + Ukraine
landmark_case: First international tribunal dedicated solely to the crime of aggression since Nuremberg/Tokyo. Established by Council of Europe Enlarged Partial Agreement — novel institutional model. Operates alongside ICC (war crimes, crimes against humanity, genocide) and Register of Damage.
key_cases: Mandate to investigate and prosecute senior Russian political and military leadership (Putin, Medvedev, Lavrov, Shoigu, Gerasimov and others) for the crime of aggression from 24 February 2022.
stats: 40+ supporting states; 25 Jun 2025 agreement signed (Strasbourg); 2026 operational ramp-up
note: Established by bilateral agreement between Ukraine and the Council of Europe, signed 25 June 2025 in Strasbourg, building on the Reykjavík Declaration (2023) and the Core Group of States process. Hosted in The Hague. Troika immunity preserved for sitting Heads of State/Government and Foreign Ministers — proceedings against the troika may begin but trial only after they leave office. In absentia trials permitted with retrial guarantees. Linked to the Register of Damage (CoE, 2023) and future Claims Commission.
legal_basis: Agreement between Ukraine and the Council of Europe on the Special Tribunal (25 Jun 2025) · Enlarged Partial Agreement on the STCoA · CoE Reykjavík Declaration (May 2023)

name: African Court Criminal Chamber (Malabo Protocol)
jurisdiction: Genocide; Crimes against humanity; War crimes; Aggression; Terrorism; Corruption; Trafficking; Environmental crimes
jurisdiction_note: Broadest subject-matter jurisdiction ever proposed. Requires 15 AU ratifications — zero as of 2026.
head_of_state_immunity: Yes (immunity clause for sitting heads of state)
landmark_case: The immunity clause — sitting heads of state immune during tenure — is simultaneously the most notable and most damaging feature.
key_cases: Not yet operational.
note: Broadest jurisdiction ever proposed. Immunity clause fundamentally contradicts the Nuremberg/Rome Statute model. Zero ratifications after 10 years.

name: Convention on Crimes Against Humanity (ILC Draft)
period: ILC Draft Articles 2019 — UNGA negotiations ongoing
jurisdiction: Crimes against humanity — treaty framework
jurisdiction_note: Not a court — treaty creating state obligations. The only major international crime without its own dedicated treaty.
landmark_case: If adopted: closes the single largest gap in international criminal law. Crimes against humanity currently have no treaty. Most significant ICL treaty since Rome Statute.
key_cases: N/A — treaty in negotiation.
stats: 2019 ILC Draft Articles; 2023 UNGA negotiations; 0 ratifications
note: The glaring ICL gap: crimes against humanity have no dedicated treaty. If adopted: aut dedere aut judicare; reparations obligation; universal jurisdiction.

name: Sudan Transitional Justice Mechanism
jurisdiction: Crimes against humanity; War crimes; Genocide — Darfur
jurisdiction_note: Juba Peace Agreement mandated hybrid court + truth commission + reparations commission. Zero implementation.
landmark_case: The tentative TJ architecture that exists only on paper — paradigmatic case of peace agreement TJ provisions rendered void by political rupture.
key_cases: Al-Bashir (ICC fugitive — transfer committed, not executed); Kushayb (ICC, surrendered 2020).
note: Tentative TJ architecture in Juba agreement — then derailed by 2021 coup and 2023 civil war. ICC Kushayb trial is the only active accountability.
legal_basis: Juba Peace Agreement (31 Aug 2020), Chapter V

name: Nuremberg Doctors' Trial (NMT Case 1)
jurisdiction: War crimes; Crimes against humanity
jurisdiction_note: Medical experimentation on concentration camp prisoners without consent.
creation: US Military — Control Council Law No. 10
landmark_case: Nuremberg Code (1947) — 10 principles of medical ethics and informed consent. Foundation of all subsequent medical research ethics. Still operative today.
key_cases: Karl Brandt (Hitler's personal physician, executed). Experiments on hypothermia, high altitude, infectious diseases.
note: Produced the Nuremberg Code (1947) — foundation of international medical research ethics. Declaration of Helsinki (1964) builds directly on it.
legal_basis: Control Council Law No. 10 · Nuremberg Code (1947)

name: Einsatzgruppen Trial (NMT Case 9)
jurisdiction: War crimes; Crimes against humanity
jurisdiction_note: Mobile killing squads — ~2 million Jews, Roma, and others murdered in occupied Soviet Union.
creation: US Military — Control Council Law No. 10
landmark_case: Ohlendorf testimony — calmly acknowledged ordering 90,000 murders. Definitively established command responsibility for systematic mass killing.
key_cases: Otto Ohlendorf (90,000 victims, executed 1951). All four Einsatzgruppen commanders tried.
note: Ohlendorf's calm testimony set the command responsibility standard. Most death sentences commuted under Cold War pressure.

name: Ministries Trial — Wilhelmstrasse (NMT Case 11)
jurisdiction: Crimes against peace; War crimes; Crimes against humanity
jurisdiction_note: Longest subsequent proceeding. Targeted civilian administration of Nazi state.
creation: US Military — Control Council Law No. 10
landmark_case: Weizsäcker conviction — civilian foreign ministry officials bear criminal responsibility for facilitating atrocities. 'Just following orders' as civil servant explicitly rejected.
key_cases: Ernst von Weizsäcker (State Secretary, convicted). Foreign ministry officials, economic planners.
note: Established civilian bureaucrats who facilitate crimes bear individual responsibility. Sentences later commuted by McCloy.

name: Jurisdicción Especial para la Paz — Colombia
jurisdiction: Crimes against humanity; War crimes; Grave human rights violations
jurisdiction_note: Transitional justice tribunal. Restorative justice with reduced sanctions for truth-telling.
landmark_case: First large-scale transitional justice tribunal to systematically apply restorative justice — reduced sanctions for full truth-telling. Innovative macro-case methodology.
key_cases: Macro-cases on kidnapping, recruitment of minors, extrajudicial killings ('false positives').
note: Part of Colombia's System for Truth, Justice, Reparation, and Non-Repetition. Combines restorative and retributive justice.
